changeLog.change: Public-release staging baseline. The compliance registers ship in a pending state: per-election ballot-order verification and the control/product-boundary sign-offs each land by pull request so the public record carries the attestations, not assertions.
2019 ballot-order verification released: two-person review of the compiled ballot order against the published AEC results (cameron-young, tara-buckley).
2022 ballot-order verification released: two-person review of the compiled 2022 ballot order against the published AEC results (cameron-young, tara-buckley).
2025 ballot-order verification released: two-person review of the compiled 2025 ballot order against the published AEC results (cameron-young, tara-buckley).

Next-election provisional comparison content reviewed: two-person review (cameron-young, tara-buckley) of the current-parliament question set and the party mapping used for the upcoming-election comparison. No AEC ballot exists yet, so ballot-order verification for the next election remains pending until nominations are declared.

Initial public-release compliance baseline. Full review and sign-off of every control in docs/legal/control-register.json (control-1 .. control-31) by the accountable signatories (cameron-young, an Australian lawyer, with tara-buckley co-signing two-person records). The standing legal positions of record: (1) PRINTED ELECTORAL OUTPUT — the National Digital authoriser model for the printed how-to-vote worksheet (s321D Commonwealth Electoral Act): National Digital authorises the fixed printed template and comparison content, and the printed output separately identifies the preference order as the user's own selection; shared links are read-only and cannot print. (2) NEUTRALITY — no candidate or party recommendation anywhere; alignment figures are party-panel-only, derived from recorded parliamentary voting, never attributed to an individual candidate; the enforceable absolute-claims register bans categorical/quasi-legal wording without current evidence-backed permits. (3) FUNDING & DISCLOSURE — National Digital is not a disclosure entity for 2026-H2 (classified electoral expenditure below the $17,300 threshold); to be re-assessed before the 2027-01-01 regime ($5,000 threshold). (4) PRIVACY — voluntary APP-level controls; research storage is aggregate counters only with server-enforced consent, k-threshold (k=10) database-layer disclosure control and complementary suppression; the earlier per-person research data was de-identified to aggregates and destroyed (EV-AGGREGATE-CONVERSION / EV-DESTRUCTION-CERT). (5) DATA RIGHTS — AEC candidate/results CSV data under CC BY 4.0; AEC boundary GIS under the separate AEC Spatial Data Download Data Licence with the prescribed derivative-product notice displayed adjacent to every map; TVFY vote data under ODbL from locked direct-API snapshots; rights domains contamination-proofed. (6) ACCESSIBILITY — WCAG 2.2 AA target with blocking automated gates and completed human assistive-technology testing. (7) ELIGIBILITY — age-first self-declaration gate with an under-18 explore-only mode. For the public release the registers were consolidated and renumbered (controls foundation-first as control-1..control-31; ADRs foundation-first as 0001..0016), superseding the pre-release internal review iterations this baseline consolidates.

Correction: reviewer descriptor changed from 'Australian legal practitioner' to 'Australian lawyer' (in the reviewer field and the 2026-07-20 baseline entry). 'Australian legal practitioner' is the statutory term for an Australian lawyer who holds a current practising certificate. The reviewer was admitted as a Lawyer of the Supreme Court of New South Wales on 13 April 2012 (roll number L12/0636) and does not hold a current practising certificate. No control positions, sign-offs or review dates change.

Anti-abuse and forms self-hosting: Cloudflare Turnstile and Formspree removed. The anti-abuse challenge is now a self-hosted proof-of-work (open ALTCHA protocol, altcha-lib, MIT) issued and verified by our own Pages Functions — purpose-bound, single-use (burned in the atomic nonce store) and identical on every channel, with no third-party script, iframe or verification call and therefore no visitor data leaving our infrastructure for it (ADR-0017). The contact/feedback forms post to our own /api/forms endpoint, which verifies the same challenge and relays the message to the operator inbox via Cloudflare Email Sending (relay-only: nothing stored, no IP/UA read, no logging). The browser Content-Security-Policy now contains no third-party origin at all; the third-party services register is empty. Anti-abuse remains non-interactive and accessible (a background computation, never a puzzle). Provider-neutrality of the challenge layer is retained (control-19).

Brand name set in text as How2Vote (BRAND.md): the product name is title-cased wherever it is rendered as glyphs by a font or read aloud, while the wordmark artwork keeps its drawn lower-case lockup and identifiers stay lower-case how2vote in every case. Terms of Use reissued as version 2026-07.2 (effective 2026-07-27) to carry the name change: the amendment is confined to the product name's capitalisation in clauses 1 and 'Who may use the Service' — no right, obligation, permitted use, licence or liability position is altered, and every clause bound by terms-registry.json requiredWording is unchanged. Because acceptance is recorded against an exact version, the bump re-prompts every user to accept 2026-07.2. The prior 2026-07.1 hash is retained in the registry so the superseded wording stays auditable. Pending validation by cameron-young and tara-buckley.
